headline: Deep models condition genomic predictions on tissue, clinical, and regulatory context
label: Context Conditioned Deep Genomics
summary: Recent work pairs genomic deep models with clinical, tissue, and regulatory context while adding interpretability and compression.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep models that condition predictions on biological or clinical context rather than on sequence or expression alone. GeMM-GAN conditions a generator on histopathology image patches and clinical text via cross-attention to synthesize gene expression profiles. Splice Ninja conditions a sequence model on expression levels of 301 splicing factors to predict tissue-specific PSI in unseen tissues. ChromBERT, pre-trained on ChIP-seq data from about 1,000 transcription regulators, learns interpretable, context-specific regulatory networks. Other items emphasize interpretability, as TPCAV applies concept attribution to genomics models beyond one-hot DNA, and compression, as post hoc SVD of the Sei model reduces size by up to 90%. The set is heterogeneous: EDEN and LaCoGSEA address sequence encoding and pathway analysis, and generality beyond the reported datasets is not established.
